character_sheet: A tameable winged stink dragon: an 8x8x10 body with a chest block and a rump, a two-piece raked neck to a 5x5x5 head with a snout and two two-piece horns, two zero-thickness 18x10 wings, four 8-long legs and a three-piece tail (StinkyModel.java:68-166, twenty parts). 100 HP, speed 0.3, 10 damage (EntityStinky.java:122-127). Beef tames it one time in two (:228-244) and its owner's click sits it (:246-254). On the ground (the synched DATA_ACTIVITY at 1, :68-69, :137-145) it wanders, follows its owner and flees monsters (:98-107) and, one tick in fifty, hunts coal ore within eight blocks and eats it with a burp (:297-299, :313-335); in the air (2 - a 1-in-20 roll on a 1-in-100 tick, a flying or distant owner, or any hit, :215-222, :277-292) it flies from block target to block target (:459-523), hunts monsters within 12 blocks and bites within 3 blocks plus half the target's width (:437-455). It burps up a coal in front of itself one tick in 1750 and farts out one of nineteen skin-dependent items behind one tick in 2000, changing skin as often (:181-190, :205-207, :542-569); it takes no fall damage (:210-213). It spawns in daylight, at most three together (:660-665; ModEntities.java:570-571). Read it as a comic dragon: the Spyro's bouncy trot and wing flap with a longer whipping tail, the legs tucked in flight.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig (StinkyRenderer.java:23; shadow 0.75, :25) on a 128x64 sheet (StinkyModel.java:168), stinky.png (StinkyRenderer.java:18 - the port draws one texture; the nineteen synched skins, EntityStinky.java:70-71, :155-163, pick only the fart drop today); the hitbox is 0.75 x 0.75 (ModEntities.java:570-571). The original's ModelStinky(0.65f) argument was a wingspeed the port's model does not keep: every rhythm's frequency is multiplied by limbSwingAmount itself (StinkyModel.java:173), so the tempo rises with the walking speed. The tail is a position chain (:200-204) - key the joints, not the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: legs: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1, at a tempo of 2.0 x limbSwingAmount rad/tick; the right rear and left front one way, the left rear and right front the other; in flight (activity 2) the front legs hold -1.0 and the rear legs +1.0, still. Wings: pi x 0.4 = 1.257 rad (72 deg) x the speed above the same threshold, at a tempo of 2.3 x limbSwingAmount rad/tick, about the wings' 0.4 rad rests (the right about -0.4, the left about +0.4, in opposition); the rests below the threshold
groups.plain: the four legs trot in diagonal pairs and the two wing planes flap together, all faster and wider as it walks faster; in the air the legs tuck - the front pair back, the rear pair forward - and hold, while the wings still follow only the walking speed
groups.math: a = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 2.0 * amount) * pi * 0.25 * amount : 0; activity != 2 ? (Rleg1.xRot = a; Lleg1.xRot = -a; Rleg2.xRot = -a; Lleg2.xRot = a) : (Rleg2.xRot = Lleg2.xRot = -1.0; Rleg1.xRot = Lleg1.xRot = 1.0); w = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 2.3 * amount) * pi * 0.4 * amount : 0; Rwing.zRot = w - 0.4; Lwing.zRot = -w + 0.4
groups.phase: the synched DATA_ACTIVITY int (EntityStinky.java:68-69): 2 selects the leg tuck; one gait group per rig is the generator's rule, so the legs and wings share this group
groups.omega_note: the frequency terms are 2.0 x limbSwingAmount for the legs and 2.3 x limbSwingAmount for the wings (:173, :175, :179): at full stride the natural periods are 3.14 and 2.73 ticks

groups.name: tail
groups.axis: y (and the chain's x / z positions)
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) at the first piece, 1.6x (58 deg) at the second and 2.6x (94 deg) at the tip, at a tempo of 1.0 x limbSwingAmount rad/tick — so at rest the cosine sits at 1 and the tail is HELD bent 36 / 58 / 94 degrees to one side, wagging only as it moves; 0 (straight) while sitting; the second piece is placed 4 px along the first and the tip 3 px along the second, each 0.5 to the side
groups.plain: the tail whips side to side with the walk, the tip swinging wildest; standing still it stays curled hard to one side; sitting, it straightens
groups.math: a = sitting ? 0 : cos(t * 1.0 * amount) * pi * 0.2; tail2.yRot = a; tail3.z = tail2.z + cos(a) * 4; tail3.x = tail2.x + sin(a) * 4 - 0.5; tail3.yRot = a * 1.6; tail4.z = tail3.z + cos(tail3.yRot) * 3; tail4.x = tail3.x + sin(tail3.yRot) * 3 - 0.5; tail4.yRot = a * 2.6
groups.phase: isInSittingPose (the owner's click, EntityStinky.java:246-254) zeroes it
groups.omega_note: the frequency term is 1.0 x limbSwingAmount (:173, :195): at full stride the natural period is 6.28 ticks; at rest there is no period - the tail holds cos(0) = 1

behaviour: Every rhythm's frequency is multiplied by limbSwingAmount (StinkyModel.java:173): the faster it walks, the faster it moves. Above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 the four legs trot 45 degrees x the speed in diagonal pairs (:179-185) and the two wing planes flap 72 degrees x the speed about their 23-degree rests (:175-177); the tail wags 36 degrees at the root, 58 at the second piece and 94 at the tip (:195-205). Standing still the legs and wings freeze and the tail is held curled hard to one side - the cosine of zero (:195, :199).

One state branch on the synched DATA_ACTIVITY int (EntityStinky.java:68-69, :137-145): in flight (2) the legs tuck and hold - the front pair back a radian, the rear pair forward a radian (StinkyModel.java:186-193) - while the wings still beat only with the walking speed (:175). The sitting pose straightens the tail (:196-198).
The head, snout and both horns take the full look yaw and a third of the pitch, the neck half the yaw and a third of the pitch (:207-221). The body, chest block, rump and neck base are static.

The takeoff is a flag flip (EntityStinky.java:220, :278, :285, :291, :441, :447), the landing the same 1-in-100 roll answering 1 nineteen times in twenty (:277-279), the bite doHurtTarget within 3 blocks plus half the target's width on the 1-in-7 flight scan (:450-453), the coal meal a block eaten with a burp (:329-333), the burp and the fart item drops (:181-190) - none of them animation events.
